title: 1751-P: Physical Exercise Associated or Not with Taurine Supplementation—Impacts on Metabolic Health in Older Women with Sarcopenic Obesity

sections.abstract: <jats:p>Introduction and Objective: Physical exercise and taurine supplementation have shown the potential to improve metabolic parameters, such as glycemic control and insulin levels, reducing the risk of type 2 diabetes. This study investigates the effects of physical exercise, with or without taurine supplementation, on the metabolic profile of older women with sarcopenic obesity.</jats:p> <jats:p>Methods: A randomized clinical trial (NCT05415176), was conducted with 35 sedentary older women (60-75 years; BMI 30-40 kg/m²; sarcopenia identified by muscle strength <0.56 kg and muscle mass <0.512 kg). Participants were allocated into four groups: placebo (GPLA), taurine (GTAU), placebo + exercise (GPLA+EX), and taurine + exercise (GTAU+EX). The 16-week intervention involved multicomponent training (3x/week) and taurine supplementation (3g/day). Assessments included blood glucose, insulin, and untargeted metabolomic analysis. Statistical analysis used a Mixed Linear Model (p< 0.05), MetaboAnalyst 6.0 and Molecular Networking - GNPS.</jats:p> <jats:p>Results: Post-intervention, the GPLA+EX showed significant reductions in blood glucose (-13.6 mg/dL; 95% CI: -26.2 to -0.9; p= 0.038). The GPLA+EX reduced insulin (-8.3 µU/mL; 95% CI: -14.9 to -1.7; p= 0.007), while the GTAU+EX also showed a decreased insulin (-7.8 µU/mL; 95% CI: -14.2 to -1.4; p= 0.010) compared to the GTAU post-intervention. Insulin sensitivity improved in the GPLA+EX (-2.5; 95% CI: -4.9 to -0.1; p= 0.033) compared to the GTAU post-intervention. The Principal Component Analysis score plot showed chemical similarity between groups post-intervention. Molecular network analysis suggests a decrease of monosaccharides, such as glucopyranose, methyl-hexofuranose, and talose, in the GPLA+EX post-intervention.</jats:p> <jats:p>Conclusion: Physical exercise significantly improves glucose-related metabolic parameters in older women with sarcopenic obesity, underscoring its role as a key intervention for this population.</jats:p> <jats:sec> <jats:title>Disclosure</jats:title> <jats:p>G.
